cards.explanation: The answer is the priest. He pays back the value AND a fifth on top, friends. That's not a refund, that's a refund with a little extra tucked in the box. The text says he makes restitution by "…adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest…" (Leviticus 5:16). And the same verse says that priest makes atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering.

The answer is True. The priest makes atonement on his behalf with the ram, "…and he will be forgiven." (Leviticus 5:16). Notice the ending, friends. It doesn't say he might be forgiven or that we'll see how it goes. It says he will be.

The answer is False. The text says that even though he was unaware, "…he is guilty and shall bear his punishment." (Leviticus 5:17). Not knowing didn't clear his name, friends. Then verse 19 repeats the point: "he was certainly guilty before the LORD."

The answer is against the LORD. He says, "If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor…" (Leviticus 6:2). Look at who gets the weight there, friends. The neighbor is the one who got cheated, yet the LORD says the unfaithfulness is against Him.

The first step is that he returns what he took. Once he has sinned and becomes guilty, "…he must return what he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found…" (Leviticus 6:4). The text starts with giving back what belongs to the neighbor, friends. The ram comes after that in verse 6.

The answer is False. The text says he must make restitution in full, add a fifth, and pay it to the owner "…on the day he acknowledges his guilt." (Leviticus 6:5). The day he admits it is the day he pays, friends. I'd say that leaves no room for the snooze button.

The answer is owner. He must "…make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value, and pay it to the owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt." (Leviticus 6:5). The one who lost the thing is the one who gets it back, with a fifth added, friends. That's different from the case of the harmed holy thing, where the payment went to the priest.

The answer is everything that made him guilty. The priest makes atonement for him before the LORD, "…and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt." (Leviticus 6:7). Look at that word anything, friends. The text doesn't shrink the forgiveness down to a part of it.
